Entries.Text: Find map objects in the loaded maps by their type, name, fields and values.
Find map objects in every map of the project by their type, name, fields and values. Maps that aren't loaded are read for the search, without being loaded.
The maps of this project can't be read.
Select a loaded map to search it.
The map selected in the map contents.
Every map loaded in this view.

The map ID or map name to search in. Leave empty for every map.

Use | between terms to match any of them, and + to match all of them.
Which of the MSB's lists to search.

The type of the map object, such as Enemy, Asset, SpawnPoint or Treasure. Leave empty for any type.

Use | between terms to match any of them, and + to match all of them.

The name of the map object, or the alias of the model it places. Leave empty for any name.

Use | between terms to match any of them, and + to match all of them.

The field to search, by its name, its path (such as EntityGroupIDs[2] or Unk1.CharaInitID) or its community name. Leave empty to search every field when a value is given.

With a field or a value, each field that matches is a result; without one, each map object is.
Pick a field of the selected map object.
Select a part, region or event to pick one of its fields.
The fields of {0} ({1}), with their values.

The value to search for. Numbers are compared as numbers, so 1 finds 1.0. A vector is its numbers split by commas: one number matches any of its components.

Enum fields can be searched by the option's name or its value.
The ends of the range, both included. Either can be left empty.
The value contains the text. With Exact, it must equal it.
The value is less than this. For a vector, any of its components.
The value is less than or equal to this. For a vector, any of its components.
The value is greater than this. For a vector, any of its components.
The value is greater than or equal to this. For a vector, any of its components.
The value is in a range. For a vector, any of its components.
The inputs must match the whole text, rather than a part of it.
Leaves out the dummy parts, such as DummyEnemy and DummyAsset.
Leaving an input after editing it, or pressing Enter in it, searches as well.
Clear the inputs and the results.
How many of the maps have been searched.
Stop the search, keeping what has been found.
Each result is listed as: map, object name <alias> [category: type], then the field and its value. Click one to select it, loading its map first if needed.
The first {0} results. Narrow the search down to see the rest.
Select this map object, loading its map first if needed.
Find these map objects in the Mass Edit, to edit or delete all of them at once. A field and value become a condition.
Copy the results on show to the clipboard, one per line.
